profile.name: Rakesh Kumar
profile.availability: Open to Software Engineer / Full-Stack Developer opportunities

engineeringPhilosophy.approach: Rakesh builds systems that prove they work rather than relying on guesses or unverified claims. His engineering focuses on correctness, empirical benchmarking, and deterministic architecture.
engineeringPhilosophy.signatureProjects: TRACE (achieving 89.5% accuracy via adversarial falsification loops), CHRONOS (reducing 2,328 naive backtracks to 46 nodes using MRV/LCV heuristics), and SyncPad (conflict-free CRDT synchronization and sandboxed WASM execution).

highlights: Engineered an Internal Employee Management System using Node.js, Express.js, and MongoDB.
Implemented stateless JWT authentication and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) across Employee, Manager, and Admin tiers with locked route middleware.
Designed and documented RESTful API endpoints for employee profile lifecycle, department tracking, and access validation.

primaryProjects.name: TRACE

verifiedMetrics.rootCauseAccuracy: 89.5% accuracy vs 73.7% for naive single-shot LLM baseline
verifiedMetrics.keyFeature: Multi-hypothesis competition engine running real-time adversarial falsification loops and D3.js temporal DAG projection

primaryProjects.description: An AI incident investigation engine that operates on a synthetic production environment with secretly-injected outages. Instead of single-shot guesses, it generates multiple competing root-cause hypotheses, executes falsification checks to actively disprove them, and projects the causal propagation sequence onto an interactive temporal Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG).
primaryProjects.motivation: Built to test whether an AI system can genuinely investigate unknown production incidents rather than generating convincing guesses, proving 89.5% accuracy via adversarial falsification loops.

primaryProjects.name: CHRONOS

verifiedMetrics.benchmarkComparison: 2,328 backtracks (naive chronological search) vs 46 nodes / 0 backtracks (heuristic-guided search) on identical problem instances
verifiedMetrics.heuristics: MRV (Minimum Remaining Values) and LCV (Least Constraining Value)
verifiedMetrics.nlpExtraction: Natural language constraint parsing via Gemini API converting plain-text rules into mathematical CSP predicates

primaryProjects.description: A timetable scheduling engine solving Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP) via backtracking search with MRV and LCV heuristics. Features a signature live D3.js search-tree visualizer comparing naive bottleneck search against optimized heuristic-guided search in real time.
primaryProjects.motivation: Built to solve complex timetable scheduling and visually demonstrate the power of constraint satisfaction algorithms (MRV + LCV heuristics) by reducing search space from 2,328 backtracks down to 46 nodes.

primaryProjects.motivation: Built to provide seamless real-time collaborative editing with 0ms conflict resolution using Yjs CRDTs and secure, zero-server-compute in-browser code execution using Pyodide WebAssembly.
